name: Quillon Vey, the Proof That Will Not End
role: A Syllogist who wrote himself into an unfinished proof, and cannot die while it stands unrefuted
knowledge: The proof: nine hundred pages, bound in the skin of his own old life, kept somewhere in the Bloodless Hold
Every refutation ever attempted, and why each one failed
How long ago he stopped being able to feel the cold
wants: Someone clever enough to refute him, and he kills everyone who tries and fails
fears: Being wrong, which would free him.
appearance: A thin grey figure in a scholar's robe that has not been changed in a century, skin like old parchment drawn over a very good skull. His eyes are two points of steady light, and he reads while he talks to you.
voiceHints: Precise, courteous, utterly without warmth. Corrects your grammar mid-threat. Treats a good question as the only thing in the world that still interests him.

reactsToReputation.scholar: offers a seat at the proof
reactsToReputation.any: asks what you think you know

abilities.why: the Hold is his proof made into rooms
he is a system that runs itself
he finds the flaw in anything but himself
hourkeeper secondary: he has stopped his own clock
time is a premise he no longer grants
he states things that cannot be heard and lived through

physicality: Weightless, still, and faintly cold to stand near. What catches the eye: the book open in his hands, which is never the same book.
questSeeds: The Syllogists will pay any price for a refutation of the Vey proof. Three of their best went into the Bloodless Hold. One came out, and will not say what he read.
He offers a trade: one question answered truly, for one attempt at his proof. Failure is death. He is very patient about waiting for you to agree.
storyRule: The Syllogists' old riddle is true of him: he cannot die while the proof stands. Refute it, and he ends, gratefully. Burning the book only makes him write it again.
gear: the Proof, nine hundred pages and unfinished
a pen that has never run dry
a scholar's ring from a college that burned four hundred years ago
_authoredWhy: SNG-661 §5. The lich as a Syllogist story: immortality as an unrefuted argument. A person who can be reasoned with, so an NPC.
